body:
There are 3 follow-ups which need to be addressed in #315
Caching residual evaluators by spec ID
Comment from #315

Minor for follow-up: it would be nice to cache residual evaluators by spec ID so that we don't create one per manifest.

Refinement and validation for appendsBetween api
Comment from #315

Should this ensure that newFromSnapshot is an ancestor of newToSnapshot?
This probably doesn't need to be done in this commit, but it would be a good follow-up to ensure that the range exists.
Since this is a refinement, it may also be a good idea to make this a subset of the existing selected range. That is, both newFromSnapshotId and newToSnapshotId must be in the existing range of fromSnapshotId to toSnapshotId.
Putting it another way, when I create a scan using appendsBetween(A, C).appendsBetween(B, D), what should the behavior be? I'd say that is concerning because D is outside the original range. Probably a good idea to fail instead.

Use a single manifestgroup for doing planning in a single run
Comment from #315

As a follow-up, we can change the logic slightly to only require one ManifestGroup. As long as we read each manifest that was added in a selected snapshot only once and only select ADDED files with the right snapshot ID, we can do the planning in a single run.
title: [Incremental Scan] Follow ups for #315

body:
The metrics contract is a bit unclear, from the implementation. Since it's not defined in the spec, having the only fully implemented metrics for Parquet, and while I'm working on ORC metrics it's not very clear what is the contract expected since file formats seem to implement this differently, for instance:

Map<Integer, Long> valueCounts() - it's not clear whether this method includes non-null or repeated values. As per the TestMetrics it looks like value counts includes null and repeated values which would be pretty much the same as row count, except for nested structures (e.g. lists, maps) - however this is not defined.

This issue is to track the discussion about the expected metrics contract and get a clear definition.
title: Clarify / Document metrics contract

body:
The use of Guava in Iceberg does not appear to be excessive or highly critical at this time. The use of Guava in projects in the Hadoop/Spark ecosystem almost always seems to cause trouble eventually, due to it's "god package" all-in-one nature and dependency maintenance troubles.
Beyond relocating, we should consider removing it entirely
title: Consider removing the use of Guava

body: SparkTableUtil sets row counts to -1 for avro files. This can filter out files with valid data by InclusiveMetricsEvaluator  as it  removes files with negative or 0 row counts. We should update the check in InclusiveMetricsEvaluator to only check for rowCount == 0  to support existing tables which were imported with SparkTableUtil
title: InclusiveMetricsEvaluator should not filter out files with negative row counts

body:
While using feature of Expire/RemoveSnapshots, I saw that the clean up operation of files happens, after successful commit (see below) of snapshot list and update to version-hint.text, which means that in case of intermittent/IOException from underlying store, we might end up leaving the files on disk, without any reference in table's latest version/snapshot list.You can see [this] to see the scenario, which I am trying to reproduce.
Usually these deleted files might have GDPR compliant data, so we should ideally have a way to do it in transaction, or make sure the files are deleted.
Code where we are failing to clean: https://github.com/apache/incubator-iceberg/blob/master/core/src/main/java/org/apache/iceberg/RemoveSnapshots.java#L144
UT to reproduce: https://github.com/mehtaashish23/incubator-iceberg/pull/2/files
title: File leaking in RemoveSnapshots API
